name: KKR & Co. Inc.
headquarters: 30 Hudson Yards, New York, NY 10001, United States
employees: 5,043 (31 December 2025), of whom 1,491 in Insurance (Global Atlantic)
summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** KKR signs for no equipment itself, but the platforms its funds control now reach every layer this corpus sells into. In data centres: STTGDC in Singapore (75%, completed 2 September 2026; it runs an HVDC testbed with LITEON and the solid-state-transformer start-up Amperesand), CyrusOne (co-owned with BlackRock's GIP since 2022), and Helix Digital Infrastructure, a KKR-sponsored data-centre and power company launched on 11 June 2026 with more than USD 10bn of commitments from founding investors including NVIDIA and Vistra. In power: ContourGlobal, which signed for 3 GWh of CATL battery systems on 10 August 2026, Avantus, which bought an 800 MWh Fluence system in July, and Zenobē and Encavis. Two large power deals were signed but not closed on 26 September 2026: EDF power solutions' US and Canadian business (about USD 4.2bn; 5.6 GW of renewables) and a KKR-led 65% of Sempra Infrastructure Partners. Its 19.9% of AEP's Ohio and Indiana Michigan transmission companies is a minority stake AEP operates.

**BACKGROUND.** Per company filings, the registrant is KKR & Co. Inc. (NYSE: KKR; CIK 0001404912), a Delaware corporation reporting three segments: Asset Management, Insurance (Global Atlantic, wholly owned since 2 January 2024) and Strategic Holdings. Assets under management were USD 796bn and fee-paying AUM USD 638bn at 30 June 2026; the chief financial officer puts infrastructure at about USD 120bn. FY2025 adjusted net income was USD 4.38bn (USD 4.87 per adjusted share); Q2 2026 came in at USD 1.63 per share against LSEG's USD 1.41. Infrastructure Investor's 2026 ranking places KKR second in five-year infrastructure fundraising at USD 100.5bn, behind BlackRock. KKR remains a 'controlled company' until a Sunset Date no later than 31 December 2026, when its founders' Series I control ends.
ecosystemRole: We assess KKR as the capital segment's most power-led data-centre investor: its own research argues that 'the ultimate limiting factor for building data centers isn't capital; it's power', and it has built that thesis into its vehicles. Helix names Vistra as its preferred power partner and gives founding investors 'priority or first look rights, to provide goods or services to Helix investments'. The USD 50bn partnership with Energy Capital Partners pairs data centres with generation, and its first campus, built with CyrusOne in Bosque County, Texas, sits beside a Calpine gas plant. KKR, Inc. places no orders. The buyers are the platforms (STTGDC, CyrusOne, Helix, ContourGlobal, Zenobē, Avantus, Encavis, and EDF power solutions North America on closing). Global Atlantic, KKR's insurer, is a second channel of long-dated capital: it buys 50% stakes in operating renewables and lends.

productsAndServices.name: Infrastructure funds (Real Assets)
productsAndServices.description: KKR's infrastructure business, part of the Real Assets line, with about USD 120bn of AUM at 30 June 2026 per CFO Robert Lewin. The flagship Global Infrastructure Investors V closed at USD 19.2bn on 3 August 2026, KKR's largest infrastructure fund. Its listed holdings include EDF power solutions North America, Global Technical Realty, Gulf Data Hub, Sempra Infrastructure, Metronet and FiberCop. Alongside it sit Global Infrastructure Investors IV (USD 16.6bn), Asia Pacific Infrastructure Investors II (USD 6.3bn) and III (USD 5.9bn and still raising), the open-ended Diversified Core Infrastructure Fund (USD 14.9bn of commitments), the Global Climate Transition strategy (USD 3.56bn) and the K-INFRA private-wealth vehicle.
highlights: At 31 March 2026 (June 2026 infrastructure overview): digital infrastructure USD 43bn committed across 26 investments; power infrastructure USD 33bn across 36 investments, both including co-investment and signed-not-closed deals
Q2 2026 call: 'committed and invested over $75 billion across digital Infrastructure and Power'
Infrastructure Investor 2026: second at USD 100,475m of five-year infrastructure equity fundraising, behind BlackRock (USD 113,365m) and ahead of Brookfield (USD 99,112m)
Core infrastructure strategy funds the 19.9% AEP transmission stake, Encavis and Vertical Bridge; the climate strategy holds Zenobē, Avantus, CleanPeak and HMC's platform
productsAndServices.positioning: Second in infrastructure fundraising globally; on the Q2 2026 call Lewin claimed that in Asia 'We are the largest Private Equity player. We're the largest Infrastructure player.' The competitors KKR names in its 10-K are categories, not firms.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Closed-end drawdown funds and co-investment for institutions; open-ended core vehicles; K-Series evergreen products for private wealth; Global Atlantic insurance accounts.
productsAndServices.roadmap: About 30 strategies are in the market over the next 12–18 months, including Global Infrastructure, Core Infrastructure, Global Climate Transition, Asia Infrastructure and K-Series Infrastructure (August 2026 deck).

productsAndServices.name: Helix Digital Infrastructure
productsAndServices.category: Data centres and power — sponsored company
productsAndServices.description: A company KKR launched on 11 June 2026 to finance, develop and operate hyperscale data centres together with 'baseload and flexible power generation; transmission and distribution infrastructure; fiber', with 'more than $10 billion in total long-duration capital commitments' from founding investors. Adam Selipsky, a KKR adviser on technology and AI strategy from September 2025, is co-founder and chief executive; KKR's Waldemar Szlezak is chief investment officer. NVIDIA is 'a cornerstone strategic partner' and Vistra 'the preferred power partner'; the Kuwait Investment Authority is an anchor investor.
highlights: Vistra committed up to USD 1.0bn: USD 500m initially and USD 500m more subject to the fund meeting 'commercial power supply milestones for existing generation assets', or at Vistra's election (Vistra 10-Q)
Founding investors 'may have certain rights, such as priority or first look rights, to provide goods or services to Helix investments'
CFO Lewin calls it a 'perpetual open-ended vehicle … where KKR will earn management fees and performance fees'; co-CEO Nuttall: 'it's a company, not a fund'
KKR formed it because 'existing Infrastructure funds carry diversification guidelines that limit how much we could dedicate to a single theme' (Q2 2026 call)
No project, site, ownership split or target size had been disclosed by 26 September 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: A vehicle built around the supply chain: the chip supplier and a power supplier are investors, and investors get first look at supplying the company's projects.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-duration commitments from founding investors; KKR's anchor is funded from its balance sheet and other managed vehicles.
targetSegments: Power generation and grid assets serving them
productsAndServices.roadmap: Co-CEO Nuttall declined to give a target size ('tens of billions'). The first project announcement is the next disclosure to watch.

productsAndServices.name: KKR–Energy Capital Partners data-centre and power partnership
productsAndServices.description: A USD 50bn strategic partnership with Energy Capital Partners to invest in data centres together with power generation and transmission, announced on 30 October 2024. KKR funds its side from existing infrastructure and real-estate strategies and insurance accounts. The first project, announced on 30 July 2025, is a 190 MW hyperscale campus in Bosque County, Texas, built as a joint venture with CyrusOne and ECP, co-located with Calpine gas generation and expected to operate from the fourth quarter of 2026.
highlights: Announced 30 October 2024 — the date is confirmed by KKR's release, the Business Wire original and contemporaneous trade press

Bosque County: 144 MW of initial IT capacity and about USD 4bn of investment per KKR; CyrusOne's own release with Calpine gives USD 1.2bn for the same 190 MW DFW10 campus, and no source read reconciles the two figures

Separately, KKR and ECP jointly agreed to take over DCC, the Dublin-based fuel and gas distributor, for more than GBP 5.7bn; shareholders approved it on 18 September 2026 (78.1%, per Briefs) and completion is expected in Q1 2027 — signed, not closed, and not described as part of the data-centre partnership
productsAndServices.positioning: Pairs a power-plant owner (ECP) with a data-centre owner (KKR's CyrusOne) so campuses can be sited at generation rather than waiting for the grid.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Joint investments by the two sponsors.
targetSegments: Gas-fired and other generation serving data centres
productsAndServices.roadmap: Further campuses at generation sites are implied but none beyond Bosque County is named.

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre platforms
productsAndServices.description: KKR's owned and co-owned data-centre operators. STTGDC (ST Telemedia Global Data Centres) is 75% KKR and 25% Singtel after a consortium bought the remaining ~82% from Temasek's STT Communications for S$6.6bn (S$13.8bn enterprise value). The deal was signed on 3–4 February 2026 and completed on 2 September 2026; STTGDC has 780 MW operational and 2.3 GW of design capacity. CyrusOne is co-owned with GIP since March 2022 and runs more than 60 data centres in the US, Europe and Japan. Global Technical Realty, the European build-to-suit developer KKR co-founded in 2020, received a further USD 1.5bn equity commitment in January 2026. KKR also holds a stake in Gulf Data Hub, 20% of Singtel's Nxera and, once signed deals complete, 29% of SK Telecom's data-centre and cable spin-off.
highlights: STTGDC: operational capacity up 25% and contracted capacity up 50% since the end of 2025, per its completion release

STT GDC launched the FutureGrid Accelerator in January 2026, which it calls 'Southeast Asia's first live HVDC-powered AI infrastructure testbed', developed with LITEON and supported by ERI@N and the SST start-up Amperesand; STT GDC 'plans to deploy this technology in future data centres in Singapore', and Amperesand names STT GDC among its SST pilots

Compass Datacenters: Compass says it signed 'a definite agreement to establish a permanent, long-term capital partnership with KKR'; trade press describes a minority interest in some stabilised facilities; no KKR release and no amount
Reported only: KKR was among the suitors Bloomberg named for STACK's Asia-Pacific portfolio in June 2026; in September an AIP- and IFM-backed group was reported to hold an exclusive window
productsAndServices.positioning: Controls STTGDC with 75% and co-controls CyrusOne with GIP — in both cases alongside a strategic or sponsor partner rather than alone.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Controlling and co-controlling stakes held by infrastructure and real-estate funds.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Reuters reported on 10 August 2026 that KKR and GIP are preparing a CyrusOne IPO as early as 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Power and energy-transition platforms
productsAndServices.category: Private markets — generation, storage and grid
productsAndServices.description: The generation, storage and grid companies KKR's funds control or hold. ContourGlobal was taken private in December 2022 by Cretaceous Bidco, owned by funds advised by KKR, for about USD 2.14bn. On 10 August 2026 it signed with CATL for 3 GWh of four-hour battery systems for projects in the UK, Greece and Chile — 526 containers of 5.64 MWh each. Zenobē, a UK battery and electric-fleet business, is jointly controlled with Infracapital after about GBP 600m from KKR in September 2023. Avantus, a US solar-plus-storage developer with a 94 GWh storage pipeline, has been majority-owned since July 2024. Encavis, the German IPP, was delisted and fully merged into KKR's bid vehicle in September 2025.
highlights: Avantus bought a 200 MW / 800 MWh Fluence Smartstack battery system with turnkey EPC for its Rexford 2 project in Tulare County, California (Fluence release, 13 July 2026)

Signed, not closed: EDF power solutions North America — about USD 4.2bn plus up to USD 0.39bn; 5.6 GW of net renewable capacity at 31 March 2026 per EDF; FERC Docket EC26-151, comments due 13 October 2026. EDF's unit has a framework with Ford Energy for up to 20 GWh of battery systems from 2028
Signed, not closed: 65% of Sempra Infrastructure Partners for a KKR-led consortium with CPP Investments (USD 10bn for 45%; USD 31.7bn EV); Sempra expected closing in Q3 2026
Minority: 19.9% of AEP's Ohio and Indiana Michigan transmission companies with PSP Investments, 50/50 between them (USD 2.82bn, closed 5 June 2025); AEP operates
Global Atlantic's insurance accounts bought 50% of TotalEnergies' 1.4 GW North American solar and 1.2 GW European portfolios; TotalEnergies operates
Lender: a USD 200m revolving credit facility from KKR insurance accounts to Powin (October 2024)
productsAndServices.positioning: Two 2026 battery purchases at KKR-controlled platforms are on the record — ContourGlobal's 3 GWh from CATL and Avantus's 800 MWh from Fluence; the AEP stake and the TotalEnergies stakes are the opposite case, where KKR funds and the counterparty operates.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Infrastructure, core infrastructure and climate funds; insurance accounts.
productsAndServices.roadmap: EDF power solutions North America and Sempra Infrastructure Partners are expected to close in the second half of 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Insurance — Global Atlantic
productsAndServices.description: KKR's retirement and life insurer, about 60% owned from February 2021 and wholly owned since 2 January 2024, reported as the Insurance segment. Global Atlantic's AUM was USD 220bn at 30 June 2026, and insurance operating earnings were USD 1,109m in FY2025 and USD 549m in H1 2026. It sells annuities through more than 250 banks and broker-dealers and about 200 independent marketing organisations.
highlights: Long-dated policyholder liabilities are invested in long-lived assets, including KKR-originated infrastructure and asset-based finance
Funds part of the ECP partnership and held the TotalEnergies stakes
productsAndServices.positioning: The balance sheet that lets KKR commit to infrastructure without raising a new fund each time; also the source of trade-press criticism of leverage.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Banks, broker-dealers and independent marketing organisations.
productsAndServices.roadmap: KKR's 2024 Investor Day targeted doubling Global Atlantic's AUM again.

productsAndServices.name: Private equity, credit, capital markets and Strategic Holdings
productsAndServices.description: Private equity AUM was USD 255bn and credit and liquid strategies USD 331bn at 30 June 2026. KKR Capital Markets earned USD 930m of transaction fees in FY2025, 23% of them from infrastructure deals. Strategic Holdings, a segment since 2024, holds long-term controlling stakes in companies and earned USD 162m in FY2025. In this corpus the private-equity side appears as sellers: Global Impact Fund II sold CoolIT to Ecolab for USD 4.75bn, closing 2 July 2026, about 15 times KKR's cost. Strategic Holdings agreed on 31 August 2026 to sell USI, the insurance broker, to Aon for USD 17.0bn.
highlights: CoolIT exit: completed
USI sale: signed; Aon expects closing in Q4 2026; KKR expects about USD 3.3bn of after-tax proceeds
Q3 2026 intra-quarter update: more than USD 750m of monetisation income
productsAndServices.positioning: Not an AIDC line; recorded because two of its exits touch covered companies.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Drawdown funds, K-Series evergreen vehicles and capital-markets services.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 2024 Investor Day targets: more than USD 1 trillion of AUM within five years and Strategic Holdings operating earnings above USD 1bn by 2030.

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **KKR is a directory of buyers, not a door**, like every investor in this segment: KKR & Co. Inc. places no equipment orders, and the purchase orders come from STTGDC, CyrusOne, ContourGlobal, Zenobē, Avantus and Encavis. Basis: the platforms' own releases, including ContourGlobal's 10 August 2026 CATL order and STTGDC's completion release. A seller finds the buyer through KKR's portfolio and sells to the platform.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **KKR has built its power thesis into the structure of its vehicles, not only its research**. Its November 2025 insight argues that 'the ultimate limiting factor for building data centers isn't capital; it's power'. Helix names a preferred power partner, ties half of Vistra's commitment to Helix buying power from Vistra's existing plants, and gives founding investors first-look rights to supply its projects. The ECP partnership pairs data centres with generation, and its first campus sits on a Calpine gas plant. For a seller that is a warning: in a Helix project, a founding investor has the first look before an outside supplier.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **KKR's 2026 moves turned it from a data-centre co-owner into a controlling data-centre owner in Asia and a prospective IPP in North America**. Basis: STTGDC went from a 14% preferred position to 75% control on 2 September; EDF power solutions North America (5.6 GW) and 65% of Sempra Infrastructure Partners are signed. If both close, KKR will control an IPP with a battery framework of up to 20 GWh (Ford Energy) as well as the data centres that such IPPs sell to.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Helix is the vehicle to watch and the least disclosed**. More than USD 10bn is committed, but no project, ownership split, control arrangement or target size had been published by 26 September 2026, and KKR's own executives describe it differently ('a perpetual open-ended vehicle' against 'a company, not a fund'). The Q2 2026 call explains why it exists: KKR's diversified funds cannot concentrate enough on one theme.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **the 50:50 characterisation of CyrusOne is probably right but unproven**. Every trade account says it, the two sponsors speak jointly, and the European Commission cleared joint control in 2022. But no first-party document read for this dossier states the split, and an IPO filing — reported as possible from 2027 — would be the first to do so.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **STTGDC is the KKR platform closest to buying medium-voltage DC equipment**. Basis: STT GDC's own January 2026 release describes a live HVDC testbed built with LITEON and supported by Amperesand, and says STT GDC 'plans to deploy this technology in future data centres in Singapore'; Amperesand names STT GDC among its solid-state-transformer pilots. No purchase order has been announced, and the testbed predates KKR's control. It is the one KKR platform where an SST or 800 VDC conversation is already on the record.

**Collection gaps:** Helix's ownership, control and projects; KKR's percentages in CyrusOne, Zenobē, Global Technical Realty and ContourGlobal today; the amount and structure of the Compass partnership, which KKR has not announced; whether Sempra Infrastructure Partners closed in Q3 as expected; whether EDF's 5.6 GW includes storage, which EDF's release does not say.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Q3 2026 results (date not announced; Q3 2025 was reported on 7 November):* capital raised into Helix and Asia Infrastructure III. *First Helix project:* the site, the power source and the supplier list would show whether first-look rights shape procurement. *FERC action in EC26-151 after 13 October:* clears the way to close EDF power solutions North America, putting a battery-buying IPP under KKR. *Sempra Infrastructure Partners closing notice:* moves KKR into majority ownership of LNG and pipeline assets. *CyrusOne IPO filing:* the first public statement of the KKR–GIP split.

relationships.via: KKR infrastructure and real-estate equity strategies
relationships.note: Co-owned with BlackRock's GIP since the March 2022 take-private; also KKR's partner on the first campus of the KKR–ECP data-centre and power partnership.
relationships.context:
KKR's release of 25 March 2022 records the completion of CyrusOne's acquisition by funds managed by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners for about USD 15bn including assumed debt; the European Commission cleared joint control. In 2026 the sponsors still speak jointly: CyrusOne's 30 July release naming John Hatem chief executive quotes KKR's Waldemar Szlezak and GIP's Will Brilliant together. The split is reported as 50:50 but stated in no first-party source read for this dossier.

CyrusOne is also KKR's route into generation-sited campuses: the 190 MW Bosque County, Texas campus announced on 30 July 2025 is a joint venture of CyrusOne and ECP under the KKR–ECP partnership, beside a Calpine gas plant. Reuters reported on 10 August 2026 that the owners are preparing an IPO as early as 2027.

relationships.note: BlackRock's GIP co-owns CyrusOne with KKR; the two are also first and second in Infrastructure Investor's 2026 fundraising ranking.
relationships.context: The two firms share CyrusOne and compete for most other platforms. Infrastructure Investor's 2026 ranking puts BlackRock first at USD 113,365m and KKR second at USD 100,475m. Both signed NVIDIA's compute-financing memoranda on 10 August 2026 and both received Senator Warren's June 2026 letters. For STACK's Asia-Pacific portfolio, Bloomberg named KKR among the suitors in June; in September it reported an AIP- and IFM-backed group — AIP being the BlackRock-chaired partnership — in an exclusive window.

relationships.note: Founding investor in KKR's Helix Digital Infrastructure and its 'preferred power partner'.
relationships.context:
Vistra's Q2 2026 release: 'Announced Helix Digital Infrastructure alongside KKR, KIA, and NVIDIA with an initial commitment from Vistra of up to $1.0 billion', with Helix described as Vistra's route to serving data centres as 'preferred power provider'. Vistra's 10-Q splits the commitment into USD 500m up front and USD 500m 'subject to the Helix Fund meeting certain commercial power supply milestones for existing generation assets, or at the Company's election'. On the call Vistra called the role 'a preferred power partner, not a requirement'.

The arrangement runs both ways: Vistra is an investor in KKR's vehicle, and the vehicle is expected to buy Vistra's power. KKR's release gives founding investors possible 'priority or first look rights, to provide goods or services to Helix investments'.

relationships.note: A founding investor and 'cornerstone strategic partner' in Helix Digital Infrastructure, and a counterparty to KKR in NVIDIA's August 2026 compute-financing memoranda.
relationships.context: KKR's 11 June 2026 launch release names NVIDIA 'a cornerstone strategic partner' of Helix. On 10 August 2026 NVIDIA signed memoranda of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to build compute-financing platforms aiming to mobilise over USD 500bn of third-party capital. The release says they 'remain subject to execution of the final agreements' and gives no per-firm allocation. KKR's co-CEOs' statement on the partnership calls NVIDIA 'a founding investor in Helix Digital Infrastructure'.

relationships.scale: 19.9% of two transmission companies for USD 2.82bn (with PSP)
relationships.note: KKR and PSP Investments, in a 50/50 partnership, hold 19.9% of AEP's Ohio and Indiana Michigan transmission companies; AEP keeps control and operates them.
relationships.context: AEP's release of 5 June 2025: 'AEP, KKR and PSP Investments have completed the transaction … to jointly invest $2.82 billion for a 19.9% equity interest' in the Ohio and Indiana Michigan transmission companies, and 'AEP will continue to operate and maintain these transmission facilities'. The joint KKR and PSP release of 9 January 2025 says the two 'formed a 50/50 strategic partnership' and that 'KKR is funding this investment from its core infrastructure strategy'. The price was about 30 times trailing earnings and the stake about 5% of AEP's transmission rate base. This is a minority, funds-only position: KKR does not sign for AEP's equipment.

relationships.note: Compass describes a signed 'permanent, long-term capital partnership' with KKR at the level of individual campuses; KKR has published no release.
relationships.context: Bloomberg reported the agreement on 5 December 2025, and w.media, confirming with Compass, described 'a minority interest in some of its stabilized facilities'. Compass's own page of 16 March 2026 says it 'has signed a definite agreement to establish a permanent, long-term capital partnership with KKR', and its boilerplate now lists KKR beside Ontario Teachers' and Brookfield Infrastructure as backers. The amount and the assets involved are not disclosed first-party. KKR funds stabilised campuses here and does not control the company.

relationships.note: Owned by KKR's Global Impact Fund II from 2023 until Ecolab's USD 4.75bn acquisition closed on 2 July 2026.
relationships.context: KKR's Global Impact Fund II bought a majority of CoolIT in 2023 with Mubadala as minority co-investor. KKR agreed the sale to Ecolab in March 2026 for USD 4.75bn in cash, about 15 times its cost per KKR's materials, and CoolIT confirmed on 2 July 2026 that Ecolab had closed the acquisition. CoolIT is now an Ecolab subsidiary.

relationships.note: Aon agreed on 31 August 2026 to buy USI, the insurance broker, from KKR and other shareholders for USD 17.0bn.
relationships.context: Aon's release announces 'a definitive agreement to acquire USI from KKR and other shareholders for a total purchase price of $17.0 billion', with closing expected in Q4 2026; Aon priced bonds to fund it in September. KKR's 25 September update expects about USD 3.3bn of after-tax proceeds. The deal is signed, not closed, and is outside the AIDC corpus.

relationships.note: Reported only: Bloomberg named KKR among suitors for STACK's Asia-Pacific portfolio in June 2026; in September an AIP- and IFM-backed group was reported to hold an exclusive window.
relationships.context: Bloomberg reported on 24 June 2026 that Blue Owl was preparing to sell STACK's Tokyo, Osaka, Sydney, Melbourne and Johor data centres and that 'other potential suitors include IFM Investors, KKR & Co and DigitalBridge'. On 24 September Bloomberg reported that an AIP- and IFM-backed group had 'locked in an exclusive window' at about USD 20–25bn, adding that 'other interested buyers may still be in the mix'. No party has confirmed either report.

relationships.note: A rival for infrastructure capital and data-centre platforms; eighth in Infrastructure Investor's 2026 ranking against KKR's second.
relationships.context: Both firms signed NVIDIA's August 2026 compute-financing memoranda and received Senator Warren's June 2026 letters on data-centre ownership. Infrastructure Investor's 2026 ranking puts KKR second at USD 100,475m of five-year infrastructure fundraising and Blackstone eighth.

relationships.note: Third in Infrastructure Investor's 2026 ranking at USD 99,112m, just behind KKR at USD 100,475m; also a Compass co-owner beside KKR's asset-level partnership.
relationships.context: Brookfield Infrastructure co-controls Compass Datacenters with Ontario Teachers', and KKR invests at campus level through the partnership Compass announced. Both were named among the suitors for STACK's Asia-Pacific portfolio in June 2026, and both signed NVIDIA's compute-financing memoranda.

relationships.note: Fourth in Infrastructure Investor's 2026 ranking (USD 87,887m), behind KKR.
relationships.context: Both firms compete for infrastructure capital and assets globally; the ranking measures infrastructure equity funds closed between 2021 and 2025.

relationships.note: Fluence supplies Avantus, a KKR majority-owned developer, with a domestic-content Smartstack system and turnkey EPC for Rexford 2.
relationships.context: Fluence's release of 13 July 2026 announces that it will provide a US domestic-content Smartstack system and turnkey EPC services for Avantus's 800 MWh Rexford 2 project in Tulare County, California. Avantus has been majority-owned by KKR funds, with EIG, since July 2024. The contract is between Fluence and Avantus, not KKR, so the link is typed 'other'.

relationships.note: Amperesand supports STT GDC's HVDC testbed in Singapore and names STT GDC among its solid-state-transformer pilots; STTGDC has been 75% KKR-owned since 2 September 2026.
relationships.context: STT GDC's 26 January 2026 release describes the FutureGrid Accelerator as 'Southeast Asia's first live HVDC-powered AI infrastructure testbed', 'jointly developed by STT GDC and LITEON, supported by ERI@N and NTU deep-tech spinoff Amperesand', validating at least 325 kW, and says STT GDC 'plans to deploy this technology in future data centres in Singapore'. In a July 2026 interview Amperesand's chief executive named STT GDC among its pilots. The testbed predates KKR's control, and no purchase order has been announced; the link runs through STTGDC, not KKR.

policyExposure.regime: Senate Banking Committee oversight — data-centre ownership and retail electricity prices
policyExposure.exposure: Ranking Member Warren's letter to co-CEOs Joseph Bae and Scott Nuttall asks KKR to list all its data-centre holdings, including 'who currently controls the company', and to explain how its footprint in energy supply and demand will not raise costs, with a reply due 27 June 2026. It cites 'KKR's and GIP's $15 billion acquisition of CyrusOne'. Parallel letters went to BlackRock, Blackstone and Brookfield.
policyExposure.mitigation: No published KKR response was located.

policyExposure.regime: FERC Section 203 — acquisitions of public utilities and generators
policyExposure.exposure: KKR's purchase of EDF power solutions' US generators requires FERC authorisation: the joint application of EDF Power Solutions, Inc. and KKR Lafayette Buyer, Inc. (Docket EC26-151) was filed on 12 August 2026 with comments due 13 October 2026. The 19.9% AEP transmission stake also needed FERC and CFIUS approval before it closed on 5 June 2025, with AEP retaining control and operation.

policyExposure.regime: NYSE controlled-company exemption and the Sunset Date
policyExposure.exposure: KKR is a 'controlled company' because KKR Management LLP, owned by senior employees including the co-founders, holds the Series I preferred stock with more than half the director vote; it uses the compensation- and nominating-committee exemptions. On the Sunset Date — the earlier of 31 December 2026 and six months after the death or disability of both co-founders — Series I control ends, voting moves to one vote per share, and KKR takes control of the carry pool.
